scope: Native Ares movement and forest-wind recording of the retained-indexed N64 renderer. Diagnostic source changes affect only a separate staged review copy; normal runtime sources and builds are unchanged.

method.origin_observer: Read VI_ORIGIN from an installed vblank handler, associate its buffer address with the frame ID assigned to that actual attached framebuffer. Record bounded presentation observations in memory; emit one bounded trace after capture. No GPU fences, frame waits or per-frame serial logging. The observer does not write VI registers or engine queue state.
method.marker: Review-only encoded frame ID in the upper four framebuffer rows. Captured host screenshots decode that ID; window chrome and the marker are cropped. The marker adds rendering overhead, so this is an instrumented emulator observation, not an uninstrumented/hardware benchmark.
method.coverage: All 241 native presentation IDs match actual host screenshots. The first 240 pictures form the clip; the last picture supplies the timing endpoint. No missing images, interpolation, synthetic walking or milestone-frame duplication.
method.timing: Every consecutive presented buffer holds for 2 VIs. The clip uses their measured 8.023242 second duration at a constant observed VI cadence. Interrupt callback timestamp jitter is at most 29.25 microseconds around that cadence. Callback ordering may produce a constant observation offset; only relative holds are used, not submission-to-display latency.
method.qualification: This Deepwood segment sustains the nominal 30 fps target in Ares. It establishes neither other-stage frame rates nor physical hardware performance. Existing pre-pacing update intervals are not display timestamps.

gif.spatial_downsampling: 750x566 captured crop to640x483 with Lanczos;256colour GIF palette.

gif_qualification: Spatial preview scaled from 750x566 to 640x483 and quantized to 256 colours. All 240 actual pictures remain; no temporal downsampling. GIF delays are 30 or 40 ms because the format uses centiseconds: total 8.020s, maximum start timestamp error 4.99505ms. MP4 retains the measured 8.023242s duration. Both are silent.
crop: Actual 1024x768 Ares window; game crop (118,91)-(868,657), removing menu/borders and the diagnostic marker. Source N64 framebuffer 320x240 passes through Ares VI presentation/scaling; crop is not a higher native render resolution.
validation: Full instrumented five-battle native review passes with 287 accepted commands, 165 enemy commands, complete 18-cell castle reveal and unchanged canonical hash 600017321675168062.
Reusable decoder reproduces every selected source and cropped-pixel hash from the initial extraction.
Removing the only raw screenshot for one presented frame makes the decoder refuse extraction before creating output.
MP4 has 240 frames and 8.023242s duration; encoded PTS differ by at most 0.5 microseconds from the measured constant VI cadence.
GIF has 240 frames and 8.020s duration; native-cadence and spatial/palette/timing qualifications are explicit.
